newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telebras up in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telebras up in heavy trade.

text.p: Brazilian state telecommunications holding Telebras rose in New York on Tuesday, boosted by political developments and a step toward ending its telephone monopoly.

Telebras was up 1-1/8 to 83-1/2, just off a 12-month high, in heavy late-morning trade. The company was the most heavily traded American Depositary Receipt (ADR) and among the most active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
A trader said Telebras and other leading Latin American stocks were benefiting from an influx of capital at the start of the year.
"There is just a lot of money going into these markets," he said. "I think that is the really big thing to note since the beginning of the month."
Telebras shares were bolstered by the government's announcement of guidelines for hooking up 11.1 million private cellular customers, a move toward opening up the state telephone monopoly.
The stock was also helped by signs that a congressional panel would approve a constitutional amendment that would let reformist President Fernando Henrique Cardoso run for a second term.
Among other major Latin American stocks, Telefonica del Peru SA rose 5/8 to 21-3/8 on heavy volume. It also was among the most active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Among European shares, Swedish telecom LM Ericsson rose 15/16 to 33-15/16, aided by an announcement it was joining in a strategic alliance with Brightpoint Inc to get new customers in the United States.
Japanese shares were mixed after Tokyo's Nikkei average closed slightly lower. Toyota Motor Co rose 1-5/8 to 54-7/8 on moderate volume.
Advancers led declining stocks by 293 to 186 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 33 million shares in late morning.
